To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

chronic HVE stimulates distal hydrogen secretion in dogs with HCl-induced acidosis, and thereby permits these animals to normalize plasma [HCO 3-] despite continued acid feeding, and that chronic HVE also stimulates distal hydrogen and bicarbonate secretion in normal dogs, and thereby permits them to normalize plasma [CO3-] despite the natriuretic effect of HVE.

chronic hypotension is a potent stimulus for aldosterone secretion, that this effect overrides the usual inhibitory effect of chronic volume expansion, and that the effect of chronic hypotension on aldosterone secretion is mediated by a direct action of hypotonicity on the adrenal.

chronic hypotension and hypotonicity are potent stimuli to aldosterone secretion and that the rise in plasma [CO2] that accompanies the HVE-induced natriuresis in normal animals is mediated by the mineralocorticoids.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of acid-base homeostasis by the renal excretion of hydrogen ion, bicarbonate and titratable acid, and the role of the adrenal cortex in this regulation.
the role of the kidney and adrenal gland in acid-base homeostasis.
the regulation of the renal handling of hydrogen ion and bicarbonate.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
chronic hyponatraemia is a potent stimulus for aldosterone secretion, and that this effect is mediated through the adrenal gland.
the adrenal cortex plays a major role in the renal regulation acid-base equilibrium during HVE.
the adrenal gland plays a critical role in the renal regulation and control of acid-base equilibrium.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the renal regulation of plasma [H+], and therefore acid-base balance, is critically dependent on the function of the adrenal gland, which is in turn critically dependent on the sodium content of the extracellular space.
the renal regulation of hydrogen ion excretion during chronic hypotonia is critically dependent on the presence of the adrenal gland and is mediated by aldosterone.
chronic HVE, whether induced by water loading or by administration of vasotocin, is a potent stimulus for the adrenal to secrete large amounts of aldosterone.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the kidney is a very important organ in the control of acid-base equilibrium, and that the kidney has the ability to compensate for the acid-base disturbance that occurs in patients with chronic hypotonic conditions.

the kidney has a remarkable ability to adapt to chronic hypotonic conditions, which is not only mediated by vasopressin, but is also mediated by the mineralocorticoid system, which is stimulated by the chronic hypotonic condition.
chronic hypotony is an extremely potent stimulus to mineralocorticoid release.
